entities.summary: Empress Jitō was the 41st monarch of Japan, according to the traditional order of succession. Born into the imperial family, she ascended to the throne in 697 after the death of her brother Emperor Senka. During her reign, Jitō oversaw the development of Buddhism in Japan and implemented various reforms to strengthen the imperial system. Her policies also led to increased tensions with the neighboring country of Baekje, which ultimately contributed to the decline of the Baekje kingdom. Jitō's legacy is marked by the continued influence of Buddhism in Japanese culture and the establishment of the imperial family as the dominant power in Japan. Despite her significant impact on Japanese history, Jitō's life remains somewhat shrouded in mystery, with many details lost to the passage of time. As a testament to her enduring influence, the temples and shrines she built during her reign continue to stand as a testament to her lasting impact on Japanese society. The legacy of Empress Jitō serves as a reminder of the complex web of relationships between the imperial family, Buddhism, and the neighboring kingdoms of ancient Japan.
